_readme: The fight. Same key as the overworld theme - A minor, no sharps - because a battle is an
interruption of the road rather than a different game, and a tune that modulates on every
encounter reads as two soundtracks fighting each other.
Faster than the theme (160 against 120) and half its length: four bars at 160bpm is six
seconds, which is short enough that a fight lasting three loops does not feel like it, and
long enough not to nag. Length is the whole cost of music here - see barred_gate's readme.
Written to LOOP, which is a constraint on the last bar rather than a setting: it ends on
the dominant (E) so the return to A at the top of bar one is the resolution, and the drum
lands on the seam. Tune.render deliberately writes no fade tail for exactly this reason.
The lead sits an octave up from the theme's and moves in eighths rather than quarters -
the same rig, played hurried. The bass alternates root and fifth on every bar instead of
walking, because a walking bass under a fight sounds like a chase and this is a stand.
